en: Manas, lion of the people, had arisen,
Do you call only that one Manas?
A hero called Semetey arose,
Azhybai and Seytek arose as his equals,
However many fenced clans split apart,
All of them struck out straight from China,
We issued the command: go there,
What hero Seytek had seen,
Khan Zholtoi had gone at their head,
The great son-in-law of rich Kongur,
A fortunate son-in-law in all he did,
What a mighty son-in-law he was,
From the tidings of the dark warrior,
A wakeful soul was here,
The hero recognized the burning words,
This was Beijing’s backbone,
This lion was its own true son,
This was his surpassing place and station,
No word could touch him even for a month,
Black Zholtoi was undone,
This was the one who had seen so many wonders.
Looking at him, he closed his eyes,
Indeed, this is the enemy himself,
On earth he encountered a spirit,
To the Burut whom the black earth swallowed,
I have gone—yet the soul endures,
To this accursed people,
Having asked, it became a robe for him,
He did not cease from asking,
When he took the lance, it became an arrow,
If he drove them in the darkness,
There was an enemy like one who had fallen upon them,
Yours became eighty-four,
What he struck against became a seal,
What he made march was swift,
What he observed became renowned,
Of the accursed Burut,
Your heart that is bent on destruction,
He himself goes upon your tongue,
Always bearing the enemy’s rancor,
The broad-valleyed Ala-Too,
It is no land to sweep across like an open waste,
The white-kalpak Kyrgyz people,
In the end, against our Chinese realm,
They are no people whose settling goes unspoken,
Three young camels stand ready at the grave,
A grieving land of the Bugu,
Bearing enmity toward the Chinese,
Those two were valiant men,
Will they lead the standard into battle?
Saying, “I will become Kenen’s companion,”
[Uncertain: He began at the prepared place.]
Summoning the Turkmen people,
He had subdued the enemy’s spirit,
With that hero Kenen,
[Uncertain: To share in prosperity together,]
[Uncertain: Without exhausting your resourcefulness,]
[Uncertain: To build it, gathering and sharpening,]
[Uncertain: Whoever offered resistance,]
[Uncertain: Striking him down and killing him,]
[Uncertain: Securing the places where blood had flowed,]
If he wished, he became a great khan.
[Uncertain: His plan was to receive them,]
They say only a little was still lacking.
[Uncertain: Is this Kakanzan any different?]
[Uncertain: He says to deceive without bending a blade of grass.]
Of Kenen in Ala-Too,
[Uncertain: Unless we beat that petty fury out of him,]
[Uncertain: Killing their rulers,]
Let us bind their heroes,
Let us lay low their champions,
[Uncertain: Let us devastate their valleys.]
When he rose against the clan,
Let us all stir together,
When he strikes them down, he casts fire,
Hearing word from the good Kiyoor,
Do not ask ill of Kiyoo,
In this world he himself is discerning,
Even in death his eyes are open,
Bearing his father’s likeness, he became a hero,
He had known surpassing fortune,
Gathering there together,
They went in fours and looked,
Covered all about in divisions,
They went down below and looked,
Wondering how his encampment had settled,
Wondering what his stratagem had become,
They went to test it and see.
His wealth and his abundance,
Lay there too vast for the earth to hold.
To that wife of Kenen,
She bore sons one after another,
She gave her sons rhyming names,
Before the birth, a seer had gone there.
As though a sovereign had remained,
They slaughtered livestock in abundance,
Finding the greatest delight,
“Let us gather the foremost horses,”
As though sharing salt with the bald man,
Meeting together with Onko,
What he had driven was enough to suffice,
Ruining seven great leather vessels,
There came a time beyond all measure,
From the mortal who stood watching.
Driving them on without sparing a soul.
They say forty remained out of seventy,
From a hundred lesser champions,
They say he took what had not been reached.
The khan-hero was left deep in thought,
The Kyrgyz stood ready to attack,
A feast vast as Nadoola remained,
What are ninety-two,
Again from his going,
What are the two who settled.
Leaving none of these cunning schemes unused,
This is the deed called speaking out,
A single fist from the bloodthirsty one’s track,
This is the deed called Kalay.
If the lone youth gathers an army,
If he pours out his rage and roars,
If Karagak comes forth and strikes,
Dust flies up to the sky,
From where does the army mass together,
If there is a din that splits the earth,
If there is an uproar that bursts the ears,
If Karala’s eye has the heart for it,
If he begins again and gathers his warriors,
If the people call it the khan’s preserve,
This deed is the black open steppe,
His musket booming—
If we do not spill their flowing blood and take it,
If the wise champion does his work,
If we do not raise one great thunderous tumult.
The hero was born by Blue Heaven,
We remained to reckon it up.
